turn_text: It's great to be with you guys. My name is Justin Anthony. I serve as Senator Mike Lee's Business Outreach Director. More specifically, that means I serve as the liaison between the business community and the Senator. Most of the time, when we're not in COVID, I spend most of the year traveling around the state to all 29 counties, meeting with businesses, chambers of commerce, economic development departments, seeking industry feedback on legislation that we're running, that we're supporting, or that we're opposing. So work very closely with the chambers of commerce to help me be my eyes and ears on the ground as it's tough to be, especially in Utah and all 29 counties at once. And so you guys just have, I'm sure you guys all know this, have a great chamber and Jamie and Vicki are just fantastic. And so really appreciate all you guys do for the community. Real quick, just wanted to run through Senator Lee's committee assignments. We did have a minor change this year of an addition of a committee, then run through four bills that I thought you guys would be interested in, and then give you just a quick rundown on kind of the state of play in DC and what this week and the coming days will look like. So as far as committee assignments, we keep our judiciary committee assignment. With the Senate going to the Democratic side, we will no longer be chair of the antitrust committee that we'll go to. We will go to ranking member of the antitrust committee, but still sitting there on that subcommittee. We're also on the Department of Commerce Committee, the Energy and Natural Resource Committee, joint economic committee, which is a bicameral committee, meaning there's both House and Senate members on that committee. Think of this committee as being a research arm or think tank of Congress. They study things like the opioid crisis, like the effects social media have on the community, housing prices, things like that. So we will serve as the vice chair of that committee now that the house will be in charge of that committee. Then the new one this year and we have not been on this committee before but it's the special committee on aging. So Senator Scott had reached out to Senator Lee asking him to sit on the committee and while we hadn't sat there before thought it would be a great committee to sit on especially with the increasing aging population we have in specific counties here within the state. So we're really excited about that, excited to get to work there. In terms of the bills that I wanted to bring up, first and foremost, And if you guys have followed Senator Lee's political career, this will be no surprise to you, but introduce the balanced budget amendment, which does exactly what it sounds like. And it's basically saying Congress has to pass a balanced budget every year. It's been a long time since we passed a balanced budget. We continue to go on continuing resolutions and omnibus spending bills. And frankly, it's not a good way to budget. It's not a good way to run government and especially when you're 20, just on the cusp of being $28 trillion in debt. So again, cities have to do this, counties have to do this, states have to do this, businesses have to do it, individuals have to do it, Senator Lee doesn't believe that the federal government should be exempt from balancing a budget. So we will continue to push for that. This one is a new bill. We introduced it first last December and just introduced it again last week. And bear with me, the name of it is long. It's the promoting responsibility over moderation in social media environments. So the Promise Act. So we've seen quite a bit of discussion and if you guys have followed the committee schedules within Congress regarding the political bias that exists within the social media platforms. And so with senator Lee sitting on the judiciary committee and the commerce committee, anything involving social media involving tech. involving privacy, all of those issues go within one of those two committees, if not both. And so what this bill does is it's basically holding big tech accountable and saying, and really holding to their promise of saying, okay, if you're saying that there's no political bias, then then prove to it and stay true to it. And so this would require those companies to disclose information about their policies relating to categories and information that they don't allow on that platform, how they moderate that content, as well as the notification process and rationale. if a post is pulled down from those specific platforms. And so again, with Senator Lee sitting on the antitrust subcommittee within the Judiciary Committee, he laid out his priorities within that subcommittee probably about two, three weeks ago. And Big Tech remained a big priority for the Senator on that. I presented on this one last year when it presented in person, which was great when we were at Bridgeland Tech. But we're about to introduce it again here and March, March 10, I believe don't quote me on the date, but pretty sure about March 10. And this one's the Global Trade and Accountability Act. This is essentially saying that the president should not be able to unilaterally enact tariffs. So we saw this in the last administration where the unilateral action on the tariffs on Chinese goods kind of sent the business community into a bit of a tailspin. And there was a lot of uncertainty that was associated with one individual being able to dictate what tariffs and what percentage a terrorist will put on goods. We believe that this needs to be done through Congress and that all 100 members of the Senate should be able to weigh in on these policies and say whether, you know, yes, this is good policy or no, we should not put in these tariffs. Again, we're not saying that something shouldn't have been done with China because frankly, it should We just believe that that action should be done within Congress where it gives more people a say at that point. There is still a national security clause in there. I know a big question we get is what if there something happens in the middle of the night and all of a sudden we need to put tariffs in place or put sanctions in place. That provision is still in there. The difference is it sunsets them. And so they get a 30 to 60 days of saying, OK, this is national security. But then if Congress doesn't pass it, if they don't vote to continue those, then they go away. So again, that timeline still being debated, but again, the crux of the bill is the president should not have the unilateral power to implement tariffs. Final one that I'll touch on before I talk about real quick and I'm watching time because Jamie has done such a great job getting us out of the 30 so I'm watching the time is the pure act which is actually built at both Senator Lee and Senator Romney. jointly introduced and very simple. And again, if you followed Senator Lee's career that this bill should come as no surprise, but it prohibits the president from established or extending a national monument in Utah unless there's congressional approval as well as state approval from the state legislature. Certain states, Alaska and Wyoming that have exemptions from the Antiquities Act, This is basically extending that exemption to Utah as well. We've seen and Bears Ears would be a perfect example where it is quite frankly turned into a political football. When it seems like a Republicans in office that the monument gets shrunk and when a Democrat comes back to office, it gross. This is basically taking away the political football and making sound policy. In terms of what's going on in D.C., I'm sure you guys have seen the House pass the most recent COVID relief bill last week. It is now in the Senate. We will be entering into what's called a voter-rama here within the next few days, possibly as soon as today or tomorrow. Voter-rama is simply you have a ton of votes coming at you very quickly and members are voting yes or no on them. the interesting part with how this COVID bill has gone about, has gone through budget reconciliation process, which not to bore you with the details, but essentially takes away the filibuster. So rather than needing 60 votes, you only need 51 votes to pass this with the Senate being split at 50-50. And theory, while the Democrats vote for it, Vice President Harris would be the tie-breaking vote on that. But Vodarama is a great time if you have amendments that you want to be included in the bill to offer them and get a floor vote on them. I will be very upfront. We have some very big concerns with how this bill is being rolled forward. One, the overall price tag of $1.9 trillion is extremely concerning. As I mentioned, we're already on the cusp of being $28 trillion in debt. another $1.9 trillion is getting us scary close to $30 trillion in debt. The other concern we have is when you look at the bill, not everything within the bill. In fact, a small portion of that bill is only COVID. The rest is kind of a wishless bill, which is frustrating to see. And the final thing that has this probably the most concern out of all of that is when we pass the relief bill back in December, there is still a trillion dollars of that bill that has not been spent. And so our idea is why are we spending $1.9 trillion when we still have a trillion dollars that's already been allocated to spend from the bill back in December? And so definitely, definitely some concerns there, but we'll continue to communicate through Jamie and through Vicky and through Emway as we get details of this bill to make sure that you guys are getting that bill because a lot can change within voter drama and obviously we're bit restricted in terms of, you know, if we pass something different than the house, it's got to go back to the house. But definitely want to be open and transparent with you guys and communicate with that. So it's 828. I finished before 830. I promise I'll be done before 830. But if you guys have any questions, feel free to, feel free to ask me, feel free to put them in the chat. Also feel free to email me. I'll put my email in there now, but appreciate you guys taking the time and giving me some time to speak this morning.
